texts.preamble: Vikas Kumar @ Vikash Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar Through The Director ... on 26 February, 2020
texts.facts: The petitioner in this case is seeking quashing of the first information report as contained in Annexure 'P/1' being Special Case No. 09 of 2019 arising out of Patliputra P.S. Case No. 573 of 2019 pending in the court of learned S.D.J.M., Patna. The FIR has been lodged by opposite party no. 2 who is the Station House Officer of Patliputra Police Station on the basis of the information received from the opposite party no. 3. According to the first information report, the opposite party no. 3 purchased from the shop of accused no. 2, Vinay Kumar, "Ashirvad Svasti Full Cream Milk'. He alleged that on opening Patna High Court CR. WJC No.234 of 2020(2) dt.26-02-2020 of the said packet a dead lizard came out of that and this fact was immediately informed by the informant to the customer care of the ITC Company. It is alleged that on next two days the officials of the ITC came to examine the matter, officials took the Vikas Kumar @ Vikash Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar Through The Director ... on 26 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123508210/ 1 milk packet and according to the informant they investigated the same. The informant alleged that when he demanded a report of the investigation from the officials of the ITC they retaliated by threatening and slapping a case of defamation against him. The informant also claimed that he had in fact submitted a complaint in writing on 14th September, 2019 itself to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Patna.
texts.arguments: Learned Senior Counsel representing the petitioner submits that so far as this petitioner is concerned, he is employed with ITC as an Executive (Marketing) and he has been accused no. 2 in the FIR even though there is no allegation against him of cheating and/or commission of offence under Section 16(1) of Food and Adulteration Act 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 1954'). Learned Senior Counsel submits that the said Act of 1954 has already been repealed long back by Section 97 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 2006'). Patna High Court CR. WJC No.234 of 2020(2) dt.26-02-2020 The main contention of learned Senior Counsel of the petitioner is that the Police has registered the present FIR not only for the offence alleged under Section 420/201 of the Indian Penal Code but also under Section 16(1) of the Act of 1954. Relying upon a judgment of the learned co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Dharmendra Kumar @ raja Vs. The State of Bihar & Ors. reported in SCC Online 2016 Patna 8301. Learned Senior Counsel submits that while considering the challenge to a prosecution launched under the provisions of the Act of 2006, the learned co-ordinate Bench has examined the scheme of the Act and ultimately held that under the scheme of the Act particularly those contained in Section 42, it is evident that the Police nowhere comes into picture for the purpose of launching of prosecution against a person who may have contravened the provisions of the Act and/or Rules made thereunder. Learned senior counsel submits that the said F.I.R. itself is not maintainable and entertainment of this F.I.R. by the police and his interference in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (34 of 2006) read with Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. Learned counsel further submits that investigation has been completed and final form has come. Patna High Court CR. WJC No.234 of 2020(5) dt.13-03-2023 Let the Superintendent of Police, Patna is directed to file an affidavit after going through the said Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (34 of 2006) read with Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, particularly, when there is a separate procedure laid down under law, then how he can justify the filing and entertainment of the F.I.R. itself. As such, an opportunity is hereby given to the Superintendent of Police, Patna that he shall justify the filing of the F.I.R. under Food and Safety law against the petitioner Vikas Kumar @ Vikash Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar Through The Director ... on 13 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131757696/ 1 and others and if he found that entertainment of F.I.R. is not correct step, then he shall come to this Court with the steps which is necessary to be taken against the erring officials. Let the Superintendent of Police, Patna be filed his detailed counter reply in this regard within 4 weeks from today.
